comparison: A tight screen-and-face image would give stronger facial emphasis but hide the physical empty chair. A doorway view would emphasize surveillance but shrink the tape image. Choose a medium-wide diagonal room view so the living woman, recorded occupant and empty present chair are legible together.
WHO: The portrait-guided woman is trying to identify an unexpected occupant in a familiar personal recording. Her poised stillness and held breath carry intimate vulnerability.
WHERE: A small lived-in sitting room makes the same distinctive chair readable in both the playback and the present room.
HOW: An observer nearby sees her three-quarter face, the CRT screen and the real chair in one continuous room.
WHY_NOW: She has stopped the tape after seeing a stranger where the chair is now empty, and is beginning to turn toward that chair.
